High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Mohan Lal Sharma and Shri Arun Sharma - Advocates f
 appellant.

Shri A.N. Gupta - Govt. Advocate for the respondent No.1
Heard on I.A. No.10292 of 2024, which is first application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C./Section
430(1) of Bnss, 2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant - Ritesh.
2.

The appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(dh) of Ipc and
Section 3(2)(v) of Sc/St Act and sentenced to Ri for life and fine of Rs.1,000/- respectively with
default stipulations.
3.  Learned counsel for the appellant contended that as per prosecution version, the incident took place on 13.01.2017, while the FIR was registered on 14.02.2017.
As per the prosecutrix, who was aged about 42 years and a matured lady with 03 children and some children being married.

The report was lodged after 01 month and in the FSL report, presence of human sperm was found on vaginal slide, though it was drawn after 01 month and in her Court deposition, she denied having any relation with her husband during that period.
Thus, it appears to be a case of false implication.

4. By taking this Court to the application for suspension of sentence, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the prosecution version itself is in the manner that the appellant used to run auto-rickshaw on hire and the victim used that auto-rickshaw for transportation of vegetables as she was carrying out business of selling vegetables.

It is argued that as per prosecution, there were 2 CRA-2693-2023 physical relations since last 4-5 years, which used to be made between two parties because the prosecutrix did not used to give fare for use of auto-rickshaw.
It is further contended that no DNA examination has taken place in the matter to conclusively establish guilt of appellant.
On these grounds, it is prayed to allow the application.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the application for suspension of sentence on the basis of written objections.
but without commenting anything conclusively on merits of the case and looking to the bleak possibility of final hearing of this appeal in near future, I.A. No.10292/2024 is allowed.
The execution of jail sentence of appellant - Ritesh is hereby suspended subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited.

It is directed that the appellant be released on Ritesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143518988/
1 bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court with a further direction to appear before the concerned trial Court on 20.05.2025 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
7. C.C. as per rules.
